title: Oaty blackcurrant pancakes with peanut butter

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a basic cupboard item, and the peanut butter is the pure-peanut kind, which counts as real food rather than a factory spread.

supermarket.reason: Blackcurrants are sold in mainstream supermarkets in July, and the flour, oats, almonds, peanut butter and seeds are everyday staples.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a frying pan, a small pan, a bowl and a whisk, and the technique is simple pancake frying.

works.reason: About 300g of dry mix to 400ml water, rested so the oats soak, makes a workable eggless batter for around a dozen pancakes for four, and the quick compote gives them a sharp, juicy topping.

honest_times.reason: 25 active minutes covers mixing and frying several batches, and the 10 minutes matches the compote simmer and batter rest.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the lemon, cinnamon and both uses of the oil, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted apart from water is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: Blackcurrants are at their peak in July and are both in the batter and the warm compote, so they are clearly the point of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Wholemeal flour, oats, almonds, peanut butter and seeds make a filling breakfast with fruit and protein, and only a little sugar.
